podcast.title: Iconic Front Person and Entrepreneur
podcast.body: Hayley Williams, the front person for Paramore, has achieved iconic status independently, extending her brand into various ventures. She launched a cosmetics line designed with Mac, which is accompanied by a TV series. Additionally, she has her own hair dye company, a line of tea, and scented candles. "She became an icon on her own with a line of cosmetics designed with Mac, there's a TV series that goes with that, a hair dye company, a line of tea, and even some scented candles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Openness About Mental Health
podcast.body: Hayley Williams has been candid about her struggles with mental health, particularly depression, which at one point led her to temporarily leave Paramore. Her openness has resonated with many fans. "Haley has also been open with her struggles with mental health, especially depression, something that caused her to leave Paramore for a short while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Philanthropic Business Model
podcast.body: All profits generated from Hayley Williams' business ventures are donated to an organization dedicated to assisting women who have survived abuse, addiction, and trafficking. "All the profits from this business are donated to an organization that helps women who have survived abuse, addiction, and trafficking."

xref.title: Early Career and 360 Deal
xref.body: Paramore, originating from a tiny town in Tennessee, signed a 360 deal with Fueled by Ramen, which had a deal with Atlantic Records (part of Warner Music Group). This deal provided them with new gear, a new van, and financial support for singer Hayley Williams' mother to continue Hayley's schooling while the band toured as she was still in high school. "Paramore is from a tiny town in Tennessee. They were originally signed to a label called Fueled by Ramen, who struck a deal with Atlantic Records, which is owned by the Warner Music Group, which is one of the major labels. Their deal was very 360."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
